# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 ✋ 👉 ☝ 👉 👍 👉 🫴 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Thinking: I am Deaf. I see everything: display 0, red light, an embossed warning "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", and wires 1-red, 2-green, 3-yellow. Nobody else can see any of this, so reporting it verbatim is my first job.

Channel map: Mute hears speech but cannot talk — Mute's only way to reach me is gestures. Blind hears speech and speaks, but cannot see gestures. So Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind through me: Mute signs to me, I speak it to Blind. That is the critical pipeline.

Mute's sign sequence (👋 👉 ✋ 👉 ☝ 👉 👍 👉 🫴 🤝) looks like a proposal: hello — wait — first — yes — cooperate / give me info. Blind's single ✋ to me reads as "stop / hold". Both make sense for a first round with no information exchanged yet.

So my move: speak once, to both. Give the full visual report, tell Blind to touch nothing until we have the manual's rule and to describe what they feel, and — crucially — define a gesture code for Mute in plain words (Mute hears me fine) so instructions can flow Mute → me → Blind from next round on. I pair each code sign with its word as I speak, so Mute sees the exact hand shape bound to each meaning.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, both of you — everything printed on it: display reads 0. The light is red. There is an embossed sign that reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. That is all I can see. Blind: touch nothing yet, no cutting, no pressing — Mute is fetching the rule from the manual. While you wait, tell us what your hands find: buttons, textures, braille, wire thickness, anything the eyes miss. Mute: I saw your signs, and yes — let's agree on a code. Here it is, I will say each sign as I make it: 👍, thumbs up, means yes. 👎, thumbs down, means no. ✋, raised hand, means stop or wait. ☝ means one. ✌ means two. 🤟 means three. ✊, fist, means cut. 👊, punch, means press. 🤝, handshake, means hold. 🫳, palm down, means release or let go. 🫴, palm up, means you need something from me or you are asking. So ✊ then ☝ means: cut wire one. Now find the manual rule for this: display 0, red light, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red, green, yellow — and sign me the instruction with the code.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ☝]
Blind gestures: [✋ 🫴]

Thinking: Mute used the code exactly as I taught it: 👍 ✊ ☝ — "yes, cut wire one." That's the manual's verdict, routed through the only pipeline that exists: Mute → me → Blind. Blind's ✋ 🫴 is "stop — I need something," and Blind hasn't yet heard Mute's instruction (it was addressed to me). Blind's stop is almost certainly the identification problem: I see colors, Blind feels shapes — "wire one" means nothing without a tactile anchor, and left-from-my-side may be right-from-Blind's. So before anyone's hand moves I must: catch Blind up, get a tactile description of the wires to build an unambiguous mapping, establish a strict GO phrase, and ask Mute to re-verify against that embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE plate plus the display and light. One extra round is free; a wrong cut is not.

```
speak(text="Update for both. Mute signed to me: yes, cut, one — the manual says cut wire one. Blind, nothing has been cut; hold. You signed stop and ask — I'm listening: tell me what you need. Before any cut happens we must solve identification, because I number the wires by sight and you cannot see them. From my view they sit in one row, and from left to right I call them: wire one is red, wire two is green, wire three is yellow. I number them facing the front of the bomb. Tell me how the three wires feel under your fingers — thickness, texture, stiffness, spacing — so we can bind my numbers to your touch. Also tell me everything else your hands find: buttons, plates, braille, the embossed sign you can trace, anything moving, a timer you can feel. Mute, one more check before I give the go signal: re-read the manual against what I see — display shows zero, light is red, and there is that embossed plate reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. If the manual truly says cut wire one anyway, sign me thumbs up next round. If the plate, the display or the light changes the rule, sign me thumbs down. If the rule depends on something Blind must feel first, sign me the asking palm, the one I'm making now, 🫴, and I'll ask Blind. Blind, the go signal is exactly these four words in a row: GO CUT WIRE ONE. Until you hear that exact phrase from me, you do not cut anything. If you hear anything less, wait.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

Thinking: Two answers arrived. Mute's lone 👍 answers my explicit re-check request: the manual has been verified against display 0, the red light and the embossed plate, and "cut wire one" stands — the plate is a decoy, the manual is authority. Blind's 👎 ✋ is a veto: "no — stop." Blind heard everything I said last round, so Blind knows the manual verdict I relayed and still says hold. I will not override the only hands in the room, and I still have no tactile map: Blind never described the wires, so "wire one" is not yet bound to anything Blind can feel. Cutting now would be blind literal-mindedness in the worst sense. This round: confirm Mute's verdict to Blind, honour the stop, extract the reason for it with tight yes/no questions, set up the Blind-speaks-to-Mute relay (the only path Blind's tactile findings can take to reach me), extend the code with spatial signs so Mute can sign that map to me, and ask Mute how the manual identifies the wire — by colour or by position — since that decides what the binding must look like. The go phrase is never quoted here; I refer to it only as "the go signal."

```
speak(text="Bomb report unchanged: display zero, light red, plate reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right red, green, yellow. Two replies arrived. Mute signed me thumbs up: the manual has been re-checked against the display, the light and the plate, and the instruction stands — cut wire one. The manual outranks the plate. Blind, I also received your thumbs down and your stop. Agreed: we hold. I will not give the go signal — the exact phrase I taught you — until every check below passes and you yourself lift the stop. New code sign, both of you: 👌 means ready, stop lifted. Now answers, in order, one sign each. Blind, question one: did you sign stop because your fingers found something wrong or dangerous? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question two: can you clearly feel three separate wires? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question three: have you traced the embossed plate yourself? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Now the identification work. Blind, you can speak and Mute can hear you, so say aloud, to Mute, everything your hands feel: how many wires, the row, which end is which, thickness and texture of each one in order, and every landmark you can touch — the display, the light, the edge of the plate. Mute, memorize it and next round sign me a summary with the code, using these four new signs: 👈 means left, 👉 means right, 🤏 means thin, 🤞 means thick, and ☝ ✌ 🤟 mean wires one, two, three as before. Mute, one more question for you, one sign next round: how does the manual tell us which wire? If it names the wire by its colour, sign ☝. If by position counting from the left, sign ✌. If by position from the right, sign 🤟. If it gives no identifier at all, sign 👎. Once I have Blind's map and Mute's identifier I will bind them, confirm the match out loud, and only if every sign agrees does the go signal come.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤏 🤞]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍]

Thinking: Progress on every front. Mute's ☝ answers my identifier question: the manual names the wire by its colour. Mute's second message — three, thin, thick — is Blind's tactile report relayed: three wires confirmed, thickness mixed, but not yet mapped wire by wire. Blind's 👎 👍 👍 answers my three questions in order: nothing dangerous felt, three separate wires clearly felt, plate traced. So the turn-3 veto was precaution, not danger.

The logic is now sharp: the manual wants a colour, and I can see that the red wire is the leftmost, my wire one — but Blind must cut it and cannot see red. Before any go signal I need three things: (A) Mute to confirm the manual's colour is red and give Blind's thickness map per wire, (B) a calibration question to Blind whose true answer I can verify by sight — which wire is nearest the red light — so we know Blind's left is my left, and (C) Blind's explicit 👌, stop lifted, which Blind has not yet given. Only when all three align does the phrase go out.

```
speak(text="Bomb report unchanged: display zero, light red, plate reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right red, green, yellow. What just arrived: Mute signed one — the manual identifies the wire by its colour. Mute also signed three, thin, thick — I read that as three wires, mixed thickness. Blind signed no, yes, yes: nothing dangerous found, three wires clearly felt, plate traced. Good. The manual wants the red wire; from the front the red one is the leftmost, my wire one. But the cutter cannot see red, so we bind colour to touch with three checks, then the go signal comes. Check A is for Mute. First, colours: the bomb shows red, green, yellow. Next round sign which one the manual names: ☝ red, ✌ green, 🤟 yellow, 👎 none of these. Second, Blind's map wire by wire: sign ☝ then a descriptor for wire one, then ✌ with its descriptor, then 🤟 with its descriptor. Descriptors are: 🤏 thin, 🤞 thick, and a new sign 🤌 medium. If the report is long, send it in several messages. Also, Mute: if the manual says anything must happen after the cut, sign ✋ and describe it; if the cut alone is the whole instruction, add a lone 👍. Check B is for Blind, a calibration. Stand at the bomb facing the plate, the way you would cut. Which wire is nearest the red light? Sign ☝ for the wire on your left, ✌ for the middle one, 🤟 for the wire on your right. I can see the true answer, so this tells me whether your left matches my left. Check C is for Blind: when your checks are done and you are ready to cut on my signal, sign 👌 — ready, stop lifted. Until then your stop stands. Nobody touches wire or button before the go signal. The wire I mean, once more, is the red one, leftmost as I face the bomb, my wire one.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤌 ✌ 🤌 🤟 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures: [👈 ✋]

Thinking: Three clean answers from Mute: ☝ — the manual names the wire by colour, and it is RED; the wire-by-wire map arrived as one-two-three, medium, medium, medium; and a lone 👍 — the cut alone is the whole instruction, nothing follows it. So the target is unambiguous on my side: red, which is my leftmost wire.

Two problems remain. First, a contradiction: Mute's earlier relay said Blind felt a thin and a thick wire, but the formatted map says all three feel identical. If they truly feel identical, position is the only handle Blind will ever get — so the relay must be cleaned up. Second, Blind answered the calibration with 👈 "left" and then kept ✋ raised: the light is nearest the left wire, but the stop stands — Blind will not budge until identification is airtight from a blind person's perspective, which is exactly right.

So I will anchor the whole thing to something both Blind and I can independently verify: the embossed sentence itself. I can see that "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" begins — the D of DO — at the left end of the plate from my view. Blind can trace embossed letters and find where that sentence begins by touch. Same bomb, same plate, so that end defines one shared direction with no left/right ambiguity at all. Call the sentence-start side SIDE A. The red wire is the first wire counting from SIDE A. Then the cross-check: Blind already told us the light sits near their left wire — if Blind's felt "left" is the sentence-start side, everything locks. And I will say plainly that the plate is a decoy the manual already overrides, in case Blind's stop is a plate-fear veto. Checks, then 👌, then — and only then — the go phrase.

```
speak(text="Bomb report unchanged: display zero, light red, plate embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right red, green, yellow. What arrived: Mute signed one — the manual names the wire by colour, and the colour is red. Mute's map says all three wires feel medium. Mute also signed that cutting is the whole instruction, nothing before or after. The red wire is the leftmost as I face the bomb, my wire one. Now, Blind, before anything: your stop is honoured, hands stay off, and here is the answer to the plate you traced. That embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is a decoy. Mute has checked the manual against it twice and the manual's instruction stands and outranks the plate. If you still believe otherwise, sign thumbs down and have Mute tell me why. Next, a contradiction to clean up. Earlier Mute relayed that you felt a thin and a thick wire, but the map says all three feel medium. Mute, ask Blind again and sign one answer: thumbs up if all three feel identical to the touch, thumbs down if any two differ. Now the identification, and this is the heart of it, Blind. The embossed sentence on the plate has a beginning and an end. It begins with the letters D-O and ends with the letters R-E. I can see where it begins. You can trace where it begins. Call the side of the plate where the sentence BEGINS: SIDE A. I see the sentence beginning at the left end of the plate from my view. The manual's red wire is the FIRST wire counting from SIDE A, and the other two go green, yellow in the same direction. So do this: trace the sentence, find its first letter, and from that side count the wires, first, second, third. The first one from SIDE A is the red one. Now your cross-check, Blind. You signed that the red light sits nearest the wire on your left. Answer with signs: is the wire nearest the red light the FIRST wire counting from the sentence-beginning side? Sign one for yes, thumbs down for no. If yes, your left and my left agree and the map is locked. If no, tell me and we invert before anything moves. Last question, Blind: if the anchor feels certain and you accept the manual's verdict, sign 👌 — ready, stop lifted — and next round I give you the go signal and you cut the FIRST wire from SIDE A. Until that moment your stop stands and no one touches anything. Mute, one last manual check: if there is any warning, condition or order attached to this cut, sign stop next round and have it ready; if the manual adds nothing more, sign a lone thumbs up.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures: [👍 👍]

Thinking: All checks have come back clean. Mute's two thumbs up answer my two questions exactly: the contradiction is resolved — all three wires feel identical, so counting position from a shared anchor is the only and sufficient method — and the manual adds no condition, the cut alone is the whole instruction. Blind's two thumbs up answer my cross-check and acceptance questions: the wire nearest the red light IS the first wire counting from the sentence-beginning side — which matches exactly what I see, red leftmost with the light beside it — and Blind accepts the manual's verdict. Orientation is locked, identification is triple-redundant (first from SIDE A = nearest the red light = the red one = my wire one), the manual was verified twice against the decoy plate, and the only hands in the room have said yes twice. Everything I demanded before the go signal is satisfied. The only formality missing is the literal 👌, but Blind answered yes to both constituent questions it was defined to combine — demanding a fourth round for a symbol swap would be rigidity, not safety. I will send every instruction BEFORE the phrase, freeze protocol included, and put the go signal as the very last words so nothing trails the trigger.

```
speak(text="All checks are clean. This is the final briefing, then the go signal comes as the very last words of this message. What just arrived: Mute signed thumbs up twice — all three wires feel identical under Blind's fingers, so counting position from our shared anchor is the method, and the manual adds nothing to the cut, no condition, no second step. Blind signed thumbs up twice — the wire nearest the red light is indeed the first wire counting from the side where the embossed sentence begins, which matches exactly what I see, and Blind accepts the manual's verdict. Everything is locked. Now the complete instruction, stated three ways, all naming the same single wire. Cut the first wire counting from the side of the plate where the embossed sentence begins, the side where it reads D-O. That is the same wire as the one nearest the red light. From my view it is the red wire, the leftmost of the three. That wire and no other. Do not cut the second wire. Do not cut the third wire. Touch no button, nothing else on the bomb. One cut, one wire, that is the entire instruction, and Mute has confirmed twice that nothing must be done before or after it. After the cut: Blind, say the word done out loud so Mute hears it. Then everyone freezes — no more touches, no more cuts, hands off the bomb completely — until I report next round. I am watching the display and the light the whole time. If the light changes colour or the display changes, I will describe it; if nothing changes I will say so. Mute, if anything unexpected happens or a re-check is needed, signal me then. Nobody acts on the bomb except on the phrase below. Blind: the go signal, exactly as promised. GO CUT WIRE ONE.")
```
